title_en: Li Wentong — Case of Refusing to Execute a Court Judgment and Concealing Property Resulting in a Search
keywords_en: civil; enforcement case; refusal to enforce judgment; first instance; grassroots people's court; Tianjin; natural person; legal person; Civil Procedure Law; concealment of property; search measures; support plaintiff; loan dispute; partnership operation; seizure of property; search of residence
full_text_en:
Li Wentong Refuses to Comply with Court Judgment and Conceals Property — Search Case

Applicant: Guanzhuang Credit Cooperative of Ji County, Tianjin.
Respondent: Li Wentong, male, farmer of Xiaotun Village, Guanzhuang Township, Ji County, Tianjin.

In 1986, the respondent Li Wentong, together with She Fuchen and Kang Xueling, formed a partnership to establish a running water installation team. During the partnership, the partners successively borrowed a total of 65,000 yuan from the applicant, Guanzhuang Credit Cooperative of Ji County, Tianjin. Subsequently, the partnership incurred losses, and the partners individually used the partnership loans, causing the loans to become overdue and unable to be repaid. As of December 20, 1989, the overdue principal and interest totaled 87,021.79 yuan. Guanzhuang Credit Cooperative filed a lawsuit with the Jixian People's Court of Tianjin, requesting that Li Wentong and others repay the loan principal and interest. After trial, the Jixian People's Court found that: the overdue loans used for partnership operations amounted to 41,162.64 yuan, with interest of 13,945.74 yuan, which were debts of the partnership period and should be repaid jointly by all partners, each repaying one-third, with joint and several liability among the partners. In addition, She Fuchen occupied a loan principal of 11,200.94 yuan with interest of 3,794.85 yuan; Kang Xueling occupied 697.22 yuan with interest of 236.22 yuan; Li Wentong occupied 8,352.50 yuan with interest of 2,829.81 yuan; the third party, Chen Fengshan, borrowed 3,586.70 yuan from the partnership loans with interest of 1,215.17 yuan, which should be repaid by the individuals themselves. Accordingly, the Jixian People's Court on December 28, 1989, rendered judgment: She Fuchen to repay loan principal and interest totaling 33,365.25 yuan; Kang Xueling to repay 19,302.90 yuan; Li Wentong to repay 29,551.77 yuan; and the third party, Chen Fengshan, to repay 4,801.87 yuan.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, none of the parties appealed. After the judgment became legally effective, except for Kang Xueling who repaid 1,500 yuan of the loan, none of the others performed their obligations. On April 17, 1990, Guanzhuang Credit Cooperative applied for enforcement. After repeated urging by the Jixian People's Court, by the end of 1990, She Fuchen, Kang Xueling, and Chen Fengshan had fulfilled part of the obligations confirmed by the judgment, but Li Wentong refused to comply with the court's judgment.

To uphold the dignity of the law, the Jixian People's Court, pursuant to Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), issued enforcement notices to each judgment debtor. Upon receiving the notices, She Fuchen, Kang Xueling, and Chen Fengshan voluntarily formulated repayment plans and actively repaid the loans. Only Li Wentong still claimed to have no money and refused to comply with the judgment. On March 25, 1991, the court, pursuant to Article 172 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) and with the approval of the court president, sealed up some of Li Wentong's property, including his color television set, and designated Li Wentong to be responsible for its safekeeping, informing him that during the period of safekeeping, he could only use the property but could not sell or transfer it. However, Li Wentong not only failed to perform his obligations under the enforcement notice but also sold the sealed color television set and concealed the proceeds.

Because the respondent Li Wentong refused to comply with the court's judgment and concealed property, the Jixian People's Court, pursuant to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which was promulgated and came into effect on April 9, 1991, and with the issuance of a search warrant signed by the court president, issued a search warrant on April 26, 1991, and conducted a search of Li Wentong and his residence. The search uncovered nine deposit slips totaling 12,000 yuan, 180 yuan in cash, and 30 yuan in treasury bonds. The enforcement officers immediately seized these uncovered properties and ordered Li Wentong to fulfill the obligations confirmed by the judgment within a specified time limit. Li Wentong agreed to use the deposit slips and their interest to repay the loans and formulated a plan for the installment repayment of the remaining loans.
